approved: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Participant Service Guarantee and Other Measures) Bill 2022
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would cut red tape and set clearer decision-making timelines for the National Disability Insurance Scheme.
It would create a Participant Service Guarantee that puts into law how long key processes can take and how the Agency must engage with people.
The bill also simplifies plan changes, clarifies eligibility for those with episodic impairments, and lets the Agency pay providers directly for participants.
The bill would set legislated timeframes and engagement principles for the Agency's main administrative tasks.
It would simplify how a participant's plan can be changed.
It would reduce other administrative burdens for participants, families and carers.
It would clarify who qualifies when someone has a fluctuating or episodic impairment.
It would let the Agency make direct payments for participants.
It would remove redundant rules and rule-making powers left over from the NDIS's transition period.
People with disability who use the NDIS, along with their families and carers, are the main groups affected.
National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Participant Service Guarantee and Other Measures) Bill 2022 - Consideration of amendments - Greens amendments

The member supported the NDIS amendment bill but noted concerns about a 4% drop in average plan values, a rise in AAT appeals from 2,160 to 3,853, and $19.1 million in legal costs in six months, while also criticising age discrimination that excludes people over 65 from the NDIS.

The Labor MP argued that the Morrison-Joyce government has delayed legislating NDIS timeframes for two and a half years and criticised independent assessments as a tool to cut participant funding, citing examples of constituents Liv Kalavasi, whose plan was cut by 45%, and Ian Waller, who lost funding for his guide dog.

The bill legislates the Participant Service Guarantee, requiring the NDIA to make decisions within set timeframes and meet service standards, with oversight by the Commonwealth Ombudsman; it also introduces plan variations, mandates representation of people with disability on the NDIA board, clarifies eligibility for episodic or fluctuating disabilities, and removes obsolete trial provisions.
